title: Alexa or Lixa
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 9:10 and Shevuot 7:9, where Alexa or Lixa says to Rabbi Mana: “We do much more good than you.” Hyman infers that he was a gentile, and the author of Erekh Milin, under Alexa, conjectures that he was a gentile judge.

notes.text: The Ketubot 9:10 and Shevuot 7:9 occurrences were not located in the returned bounded research. The supplied locators remain, and the textual question stays held. Gentile identity is Hyman’s inference; the gentile-judge proposal belongs to Erekh Milin.

In the Guggenheimer edition, the parallels on collecting a debt in the debtor’s absence are Ketubot 9:8, with the name Alexa, and Shevuot 7:7, with Lixa. Shevuot explicitly has Lixa speak before Rabbi Mana. The Hebrew in Guggenheimer’s Ketubot can give the opening speech to Rabbi Mana, while its English follows Shevuot. Machon Mamre’s Ketubot has Alexa speak to Rabbi Mana. Rapoport’s Erekh Milin (Prague, 1852, pp. 63–65) uses Hyman’s section numbering and argues for a gentile judge from the legal dialogue. That is Rapoport’s interpretation.
